evidence.title: That first novel
evidence.author: Buchi Emecheta
excerpts: Having one's first novel published is not as glamorous an affair as the media makes readers believe.
The would-be author would start by convincing himself, that 'this is it, this is what I want to do, I must write, I must tell a story or do nothing else.
It is novel writing for me, no matter how long it takes, no matter whether I'm published or not.

evidence.title: Verne's First Novel Finally in English
evidence.author: Eric S. Rabkin
excerpts: RabkinA Priest in 1835 is the first novel written by Jules Verne, who is for many the crucial father of science fiction.
Written in the 1840s and finished when Verne was still  teenager, the novel went unpublished until 1992, and for good reason.
Taken as  whole, it is neither  good novel nor  voyage extraordinaire like Verne's most famous and influential works.
The current edition, smartly translated by Daniele Chatelain and the late George Slusser, finally makes A Priest in 1835 available in English.

For the casual reader, it is an uneven historical curiosity; for the Verne scholar, it is rich, revelatory, and provocative.This is among the latest offerings in the laudable Palik Series, which is edited by Brian Taves and designed to bring  the Anglophone public [...] hitherto unknown Verne tales.
Like other Palik books, A Priest in 1835 is amply and helpfully illustrated.
The first illustration is  photo of the title page of the manuscript, stamped by its repository, Bibliotheque Municipale Nantes, and showing in Verne's own clear hand the title, Un pretre en 1835.
But the narrative action, taking place mostly in Nantes (Verne's birthplace) in 1829 and 1839, led Robin  issue his pioneering French edition as Un pretre en 1839.

How could an editor retitle  book?Robin, who sees the novel as unfinished, takes the title  want revision that Verne himself, who apparently never tried  have the manuscript published, simply didn't attempt.
Chatelain and Slusser see the book as an apparently unfinished novel in which the reader, like the character Michel Randeau, becomes  detective who must discover what is missing.
In weaving the fabric from 1829  1839, Verne leaves key silences, as the editors call his narrative gaps.

evidence.title: How to Write a Damn Good Novel
evidence.author: James N Frey
excerpts: Written in a clear, crisp, accessible style, this book is perfect for beginners as well as professional writers who need a crash course in the down-to-earth basics of storytelling.
Talent and inspiration can't be taught, but Frey does provide scores of helpful suggestions and sensible rules and principles.

An international bestseller, How to Write a Damn Good Novel will enable all writers to face that intimidating first page, keep them on track when they falter, and help them recognize, analyze, and correct the problems in their own work.

evidence.title: How the Steel Was Tempered
excerpts: How the Steel Was Tempered (Russian: Как закалялась сталь, romanized: Kak zakalyalas stal) or The Making of a Hero, is a socialist realist novel written by Nikolai Ostrovsky (1904–1936).
With 36.4 million copies sold, it is one of the best-selling books of all time and the best-selling book in the Russian language.

evidence.title: The Professor (novel)
excerpts: It was written in 1846 before Jane Eyre, but was rejected by many publishing houses.
It was eventually published, posthumously, in 1857, with the approval of Charlotte Brontë's widower, Arthur Bell Nicholls, who took on the task of reviewing and editing the text.

evidence.title: How Late It Was, How Late
excerpts: How Late It Was, How Late is a 1994 stream-of-consciousness novel written by Scottish writer James Kelman.
The Glasgow-centred work is written in a working-class Scottish dialect, and follows Sammy, a shoplifter and ex-convict.

evidence.title: The Alchemist (novel)
excerpts: The Alchemist (Portuguese: O Alquimista) is a novel by Brazilian author Paulo Coelho which was first published in 1988.
Originally written in Portuguese, it became a widely translated international bestseller.
The story follows Santiago, a shepherd boy, in his journey across North Africa to the Egyptian pyramids after he dreams of finding treasure there.
It has since been translated into more than 65 languages and has sold more than 150 million copies worldwide.
